speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing sudden onset abdominal pain; to help me narrow down the cause, please describe exactly where the pain is located and how it feels. How long has this pain been present, and have you noticed any fever, nausea, vomiting, or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ischemic Colitis.

The patient's age, history of recent myocardial infarction, sudden onset of left-sided (or generalized) pain, and bloody diarrhea are classic signs of ischemic colitis. I will confirm this by checking the results of the recent CT scan if available, otherwise I will proceed with a digital rectal exam to assess the nature of the bleeding.
